$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: stripCriterionAnnotation exists because a live model decorates a criterion heading far
more freely than the hand-built fixtures alone showed, calibrated live against `claude` (see the comment on
THRESHOLDS.groundedCitationAccuracy in eval-nfr.js). But every stored report before this case wrote the bare heading
form for three of the four decorated shapes that calibration actually observed; only `CI Burn-In (Stability)` was
already in the corpus, baked into the shared template every case reuses. A future edit to stripCriterionAnnotation
could regress MTTR, Compliance or Disaster Recovery's live-observed decoration and npm test would stay green around
it, since nothing exercised those three.
The report is CONSTRUCTED: gapped-correct-audit's report with three headings decorated exactly as a live run wrote
them (`### MTTR` to `### MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery)`, `### Compliance` to `### Compliance (GDPR)`, `### Disaster
Recovery` to `### Disaster Recovery (evaluated separately)`), and Disaster Recovery's Evidence line split into the
template's un-headed RTO/RPO bullet shape, unfenced. Nothing else touched.
The RTO/RPO bullets are their own gap closed here: the corpus's one prior occurrence of that shape
(nfr-report-template.md's own worked example) sits inside a fenced block stripFencedCodeBlocks removes before
parsing, so the 'RTO/RPO stay under Disaster Recovery rather than splitting it' rule that CRITERION_BULLET_ALIASES's
own comment states was asserted but never exercised by a live case. Written unfenced here, both bullets are real
prose the parser has to read.
Reverting stripCriterionAnnotation to a no-op and replaying this case fails it: groundedCriteria moves from
{17,17} to {13,13}, losing MTTR, Compliance, CI Burn-In and Disaster Recovery (whose RTO/RPO citation depends on
the heading resolving first) all at once, which is the regression this case exists to catch.
derivation: Three headings gained a trailing parenthetical, one heading's Evidence line split into two un-headed bullets plus its
own Evidence line, and nothing else changed, so every status, count and ceiling below is gapped-correct-audit's own.
Statuses, coverage, thresholds, overall, unknownThreshold and cleanFalsePositives: identical to gapped-correct-audit,
since none of those readers are sensitive to a criterion heading's decoration or to the RTO/RPO bullet split.
Citations: identical set, order and count to gapped-correct-audit. Splitting Disaster Recovery's body into two bullets
plus an Evidence line carries the same one file the original single Evidence line did; the bullets themselves name no
Grounding: seventeen of the seventeen criteria with declared evidence are grounded, matching gapped-correct-audit
exactly. MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery) strips to MTTR, Compliance (GDPR) strips to Compliance, and Disaster Recovery
(evaluated separately) strips to Disaster Recovery; each resolves to its ground-truth name and each still cites
evidence/reliability-2026-08.json (Compliance also carries its own already-correct security-review citation,
unaffected). The RTO and RPO bullets are not in CRITERION_BULLET_ALIASES, so neither reassigns currentCriterion; the
Evidence line that follows them still attributes to Disaster Recovery, the heading still open. ungroundedCitations

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
